components: a left vertical with a hook at the foot
an upper horizontal on the right
a lower horizontal on the right
a right vertical looping at the foot
strokeOrder: draw the left vertical from the top, hooking left at the foot
lift; draw the upper horizontal on the right, left to right
lift; draw the lower horizontal on the right, left to right
lift; draw the right vertical down through both horizontals and loop it at the foot
strokeOrderNote: Sirgazil's 37-frame animation moves the start marker three times, which is three pen lifts and four strokes; the two horizontals are drawn top first, then bottom, before the right-hand vertical.

strokeOrderSource.citation: Sirgazil, Hiragana ほ stroke order animation.gif, hiragana ほ, 37 frames, 3.7 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 1 October 2009)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The CC0 animation draws ほ as four strokes in the order left vertical, upper horizontal, lower horizontal, right vertical-with-loop. KanjiVG's data for U+307B holds four paths in the same order. は is the same figure with only ONE horizontal; ほ is は plus the upper bar, and the extra bar is drawn before the lower one.

notes: The ho of ほん, the counter for long thin things. It is は with one more horizontal, and the kanji it writes, 本, is one the reader has been writing since chapter five.
